## fb1e79984e59

**Reproduced lesson-level shortcut — numeric color order.** Generator SHA `353ce05e9e36701cbd2e3cd2f64a345c5949b25b972963fa0f43e72d836bdbf6`; executed rule hash `392773ffe271`.

The six-step schedule correctly guarantees an all-distinct ring pattern and an outer/inner repeated-ring pattern in every three-demo window. That separates successor and positional-depth rotations, but it does not control the accidental order of the sampled color values. The rival “sort distinct ring colors numerically, then map each to its cyclic predecessor” survived and disagreed with the query in 33 of 720 tested windows (40 seeds × 3 bands × 6 starts).

Concrete ordinary lesson: difficulty `easy`, seed `1`, samples `2..5`. Demo ring sequences are `[9,5,6]`, `[0,1,1]`, and `[4,2,4]`; in all three, numeric-sorted predecessor happens to equal the authority. Query rings are `[5,4,0]`, where the rival differs from the authority in all 42 cells. All four inputs were emitted by the unmodified default generator and pass its validator. The Python authority mirror was independently checked against Racket on 60/60 generated inputs. Evidence: `checks/audit/fb1e79984e59/lesson_inputs.json`, `lesson_meta.json`, `lesson_racket.json`, `lesson_rival.json`, and aggregate `analysis.json`.

This target was audited only and left unchanged. A repair should schedule color-order permutations, not just ring grammars, or resample a lesson until at least one demonstration distinguishes outer-to-inner first-occurrence order from numeric sorted order.
